summary: Defines procedures and messages for providing BGP-based services over Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6), including Layer 3 VPN, Ethernet VPN, and Internet services. It builds on BGP/MPLS IP VPNs (RFC 4364) and BGP MPLS-Based Ethernet VPN (RFC 7432), replacing MPLS labels with SRv6 mechanisms. It is a standards-track specification.

plainLanguage.summary: Companies often rent private lanes on a shared network. This explains how to offer those private lanes using IPv6 addresses as the road directions instead of the older label stickers.

subtitle: How BGP tells edge routers which IPv6 address to send each customer's traffic to, so VPNs can ride on SRv6.

tldr.problem: BGP-based VPN and Internet services were built around MPLS labels. Networks that run Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6) need a way to signal the service a packet belongs to using IPv6 addresses instead.
tldr.mechanism: The egress PE attaches an SRv6 Service SID to each service route inside two new TLVs (SRv6 L3 Service and SRv6 L2 Service) of the BGP Prefix-SID attribute. The ingress PE wraps customer packets in an outer IPv6 header addressed to that SID.
tldr.outcome: L3VPN, EVPN and Internet services can run over an SRv6 core using ordinary BGP machinery, with the underlay needing only plain IPv6 forwarding for best-effort service. The RFC has been updated by RFC 9819.

today: RFC 9252 is a Proposed Standard published in July 2022. It has been updated by RFC 9819 and has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Overlay Services on an SRv6 Core
sections.content:
SRv6 means Segment Routing instantiated on the IPv6 data plane. BGP is used to advertise the reachability of the prefixes of a service from an egress Provider Edge (PE) to ingress PE nodes. This RFC defines procedures and messages for SRv6-based BGP services: Layer 3 VPN (L3VPN), Ethernet VPN (EVPN) and Internet services. It builds on RFC 4364 and RFC 7432.

The key object is the SRv6 Service SID: an SRv6 Segment Identifier tied to a service-specific endpoint behavior on the advertising PE, such as End.DT (look up in the VRF table) or End.DX (cross-connect to a next hop). The egress PE signals the SID along with the service route. The ingress PE encapsulates the payload in an outer IPv6 header whose destination address is that SID. For best-effort connectivity the underlay between the PEs only needs plain IPv6 forwarding.

For service with an underlay Service Level Agreement, the egress PE colors the route with a Color Extended Community. The ingress PE then encapsulates the packet with the SR Policy segment list and the Service SID using the Segment Routing Header (SRH). Underlay nodes whose SIDs are in that list MUST support the SRv6 data plane.
sections.plainLanguage: Instead of putting a sticker on each parcel to say which customer it is for, the sender writes the customer's special address on the outside. The router at the far end reads that address and knows what to do.

sections.title: The SRv6 Service TLVs and Sub-TLVs
sections.content:
The RFC extends the BGP Prefix-SID attribute with two new TLVs. The SRv6 L3 Service TLV (type 5) plays the role an MPLS label plays on a Layer 3 service route. The SRv6 L2 Service TLV (type 6) does the same for EVPN route types for Layer 2 services. Each TLV has a 1-octet type, a 2-octet length, a 1-octet reserved field (set to 0 by the sender, ignored by the receiver) and a list of Sub-TLVs.

The only Sub-TLV defined is the SRv6 SID Information Sub-TLV (type 1). It carries a 16-octet SRv6 SID value, one octet of Service SID Flags (none are defined, so it MUST be 0), a 2-octet SRv6 Endpoint Behavior and further Sub-Sub-TLVs. The opaque behavior value 0xFFFF MAY be used when the advertiser wants to hide the real behavior. A receiver must not treat an unrecognized behavior as invalid, except for behaviors that use arguments. When several SID Information Sub-TLVs are present, the ingress PE SHOULD use the first.

When a speaker re-advertises a route with the next hop unchanged, it SHOULD propagate the TLVs, including unrecognized types. If the next hop is changed, the TLVs SHOULD be updated with the locally allocated SID, and unrecognized Sub-TLVs and Sub-Sub-TLVs MUST be removed.
sections.plainLanguage: The announcement is like a form with labelled boxes. One box holds the special address, another says what the receiver should do with parcels sent there. Boxes the reader does not understand get passed along or thrown out depending on who is handing them on.

sections.title: The SID Structure and the Transposition Scheme
sections.content:
The SRv6 SID Structure Sub-Sub-TLV (type 1, length 6 octets) says how long each part of the SID is, in bits: Locator Block, Locator Node, Function and Argument. It also carries a Transposition Length and a Transposition Offset.

These two fields support the Transposition Scheme. Some services, such as EVPN VPWS, need a different SID for each route, which would pack badly into BGP updates. With transposition, only the common part of the SID (for example the locator) goes in the SRv6 Service TLV, and the variable part (the Function or Argument) is placed in the existing MPLS Label field of the NLRI. The receiver reassembles the full SID. Use of the scheme is RECOMMENDED where the service encoding allows it. The bits moved out MUST be set to 0 in the SID value, and a Transposition Length of 0 means nothing is transposed.

The sum of the four part lengths MUST be at most 128 and greater than the sum of offset and length. As an example, if the Locator Block and Node total 64 bits and a 16-bit Function is fully transposed, the offset is 64 and the length is 16. Label fields limit what fits: 20 bits in RFC 4364 and RFC 8277, and 24 bits in RFC 7432.

Because a BGP speaker without this support may misread the transposed bits as an MPLS label, implementations MUST provide a way to control advertisement of SRv6-based service routes per neighbor and per service.
sections.plainLanguage: Imagine a long phone number where most digits are the same for everyone. To save space, you write the shared part once and tuck just the last few digits into a small box on each message. The reader joins them back together.

sections.title: L3 Services over an SRv6 Core
sections.content:
Egress PEs advertise overlay service prefixes with a Service SID in an SRv6 L3 Service TLV. The TLV tells the ingress PE two things: the egress PE supports SRv6 overlay, so the ingress PE MUST perform IPv6 encapsulation and insert an SRH when required, and which SID to use. The SID has only local significance at the egress PE, where it may be allocated per CE or per VRF. It SHOULD be routable within the AS of the egress PE.

For shortest-path steering, the ingress PE encapsulates the customer packet in an outer IPv6 header using the H.Encaps or H.Encaps.Red flavors from RFC 8986. It MUST check that the Service SID is resolvable before considering the route for best path computation. The egress PE sets the BGP next hop to one of its IPv6 addresses.

The RFC covers four cases: IPv4 VPN, IPv6 VPN, global IPv4 and global IPv6. The expected endpoint behaviors are End.DX4, End.DT4 and End.DT46 for IPv4, and End.DX6, End.DT6 and End.DT46 for IPv6. For the VPN cases, the 20-bit label value is set to part of the Function when transposition is used, and otherwise to Implicit NULL.
sections.plainLanguage: The far-end router says, "send parcels for this customer to this exact address." The near-end router wraps each parcel in a bigger envelope with that address, after checking it knows how to reach it.

sections.title: Ethernet VPN Routes over SRv6
sections.content:
For EVPN, Service SIDs are advertised with Route Types 1 (Ethernet Auto-Discovery), 2 (MAC/IP Advertisement), 3 (Inclusive Multicast Ethernet Tag) and 5 (IP Prefix). The ingress PE encapsulates the customer Ethernet frame with the H.Encaps.L2 or H.Encaps.L2.Red flavors.

  • Ethernet A-D per ES: the 24-bit ESI Label field can carry part of the Argument; the behavior SHOULD be End.DT2M.
  • Ethernet A-D per EVI: the Function goes in the 24-bit label; the behavior SHOULD be End.DX2, End.DX2V or End.DT2U.
  • MAC/IP Advertisement: Label1 pairs with the L2 Service TLV (End.DX2 or End.DT2U). With MAC+IP, Label2 can pair with an L3 Service TLV.
  • Inclusive Multicast: the SHOULD behavior is End.DT2M. With ESI-based filtering, the ESI Filtering Argument from Route Type 1 SHOULD be merged by bitwise OR with the End.DT2M SID. With local-bias it SHOULD NOT be merged.
  • IP Prefix: uses the L3 Service TLV with End.DT4, End.DT6, End.DT46, End.DX4 or End.DX6.

Route Type 4 (Ethernet Segment) and Route Types 6, 7 and 8 do not carry SRv6 Service TLVs. Multicast VPN services and multicast trees as P-tunnels are out of scope.
sections.plainLanguage: Different kinds of announcements, like "I can reach this machine" or "I handle party-line broadcasts", each get their own door address. Some announcements do not need one at all.

sections.title: Error Handling
sections.content:
Errors while processing the TLVs SHOULD be logged. If several SRv6 L3 Service TLVs appear, all but the first MUST be ignored, and likewise for the L2 Service TLV. A TLV is malformed if its length is less than 1, is inconsistent with the Prefix-SID attribute length, or any Sub-TLV is malformed. An SID Information Sub-TLV is also malformed if its length is less than 21.

An unrecognized type is not malformed, and failing semantic validation of a value does not make a TLV malformed. When at least one malformed SRv6 Service TLV is present, the treat-as-withdraw action from RFC 7606 MUST be performed.

The SID value is invalid if the transposition length exceeds the label field size or the Section 3.2.1 conditions fail. A path with a Prefix-SID attribute lacking any valid SRv6 SID information MUST be considered ineligible during best path selection for that prefix.
sections.plainLanguage: If a form is filled in so badly the reader cannot make sense of it, the reader treats the message as if it had been cancelled. If the form is merely unfamiliar, the reader keeps it.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content:
In the BGP Prefix-SID TLV Types subregistry, value 5 is the SRv6 L3 Service TLV and value 6 the SRv6 L2 Service TLV. Value 4 is marked Deprecated: it was the SRv6-VPN SID TLV from earlier drafts, used by early implementations and replaced by the two new TLVs.

IANA also created the SRv6 Service Sub-TLV Types subregistry (1 is the SRv6 SID Information Sub-TLV; 0 and 255 are Reserved) and the SRv6 Service Data Sub-Sub-TLV Types subregistry (1 is the SRv6 SID Structure Sub-Sub-TLV). Ranges 1-127 and 255 use IETF Review, and 128-254 use First Come First Served. A new BGP SRv6 Service SID Flags registry has all 8 bit positions unassigned.
sections.plainLanguage: A central list of codes was set up so everyone uses the same number for the same thing, and an old, abandoned number was marked so nobody reuses it.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC adds no new BGP session security concerns and introduces no new services or NLRI types, so the security considerations of the underlying services apply. RFC 8669 discusses preventing leaks of the BGP Prefix-SID attribute outside the SR domain. A filtering mistake could expose Service SIDs to outsiders, but exploiting that is mitigated by SRv6 data plane protections.

SRv6 operates within a trusted SR domain. An operator deploying SRv6 MUST follow Section 7 of RFC 8754 for infrastructure access control lists and the recommendations in BCP 38 and BCP 84. A single ACL covering the SRv6 Block on border interfaces is sufficient to block outside packets to SIDs in the domain, and an SRH HMAC TLV is an option for validation.
sections.plainLanguage: The delivery system only works inside the company's own gated site. Guards at the gate drop any outside parcel addressed to an inside door number.

fields.name: TLV Type
fields.desc: 5 for the SRv6 L3 Service TLV, 6 for the SRv6 L2 Service TLV.

fields.name: TLV Length
fields.desc: Total length in octets of the TLV Value.

fields.name: RESERVED
fields.desc: Set to 0 by the sender, ignored by the receiver.

fields.name: Locator Block Length
fields.desc: Length in bits of the Locator Block.

fields.name: Locator Node Length
fields.desc: Length in bits of the Locator Node.

fields.name: Function Length
fields.desc: Length in bits of the Function.

fields.name: Argument Length
fields.desc: Length in bits of the Argument.

fields.name: Transposition Length
fields.desc: Bits moved into the MPLS Label field.

fields.name: Transposition Offset
fields.desc: Bit position of the moved part in the SID.
